title: Large departments
prompt: Show each department_id with at least 3 employees, and the count as staff. Replace the ___.
starterSql:
SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff
FROM employees
GROUP BY department_id
HAVING ___;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET department_id = 5 WHERE id = 14;

solutions: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;
SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Repeat customers
prompt: Show the customer_id of customers with more than one order.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;
SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1;

title: Filter both ways
prompt: Using only shipped orders, show the customer_id of customers with at least 2 of them, and the count as shipped.
hints: WHERE for rows, HAVING for groups.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 7, '2024-04-01', 'shipped');

solutions: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS shipped FROM orders WHERE status = 'shipped' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS shipped FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS shipped FROM orders WHERE status = 'shipped' GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Strong courses
prompt: Show each course_id with an average grade of at least 80, and the average rounded to 1 decimal as average.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET grade = 95 WHERE id = 13;

solutions: SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id HAVING AVG(grade) >= 80;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments WHERE grade >= 80 GROUP BY course_id;
SELECT course_id, ROUND(AVG(grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id;

title: Fully recorded cities
prompt: Show each city where no rainfall reading is missing.
solutions: SELECT city FROM readings GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) = COUNT(rainfall_mm);

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM readings WHERE rainfall_mm IS NOT NULL;

title: Fix the filter
prompt: This should show each department_id with a total salary above 200000 as total, but it fails because an aggregate is in WHERE. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total
FROM employees
WHERE SUM(salary) > 200000
GROUP BY department_id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 210000 WHERE id = 11;

solutions: SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING SUM(salary) > 200000;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) AS total FROM employees WHERE salary > 200000 GROUP BY department_id;

title: Duplicate days
prompt: A user sometimes has two sessions on one day. Show each user_id and session_date with more than one session.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 8, '2024-03-02', 5, 'web');

solutions: SELECT user_id, session_date FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id, session_date HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT user_id, session_date FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
SELECT user_id, session_date FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id, session_date;

title: Big-ticket categories
prompt: Considering only products costing over 2 to make, show each category with an average price above 15, and that average as average_price.
hints: WHERE on cost, HAVING on average price.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE products SET price = 16.0, cost = 3.0 WHERE id = 8; INSERT INTO products VALUES (10, 'Pot', 'Kitchen', 90.0, 1.0);

solutions: SELECT category, AVG(price) AS average_price FROM products WHERE cost > 2 GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 15;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, AVG(price) AS average_price FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 15;
SELECT category, AVG(price) AS average_price FROM products WHERE cost > 2 GROUP BY category;
